stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 significantly boosts Gemma 4 performance on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when integrated with coding agents (Aider benchmark).

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically optimized for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This update specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling a push for optimized local AI experiences on macOS.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, both locally and in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: New security vulnerability identified in autonomous, persistent AI coding agents.
Attacks can be distributed across multiple pull requests (PRs) over time, leveraging codebase persistence.
Introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study the safe deployment of capable but potentially untrusted AI.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper introduces LACUNA, a new testbed designed to rigorously evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
It addresses a critical security issue where Large Language Models memorize sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, failing to verify true knowledge erasure within the model parameters.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log alerting, JSON repair).
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses current limitations of relying on LLM APIs, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long input contexts.
Introduces 'ReContext' (Recursive Evidence Replay), a training-free inference method designed to improve long-context reasoning.
Highlights the gap between LLMs' ability to access long contexts and their actual capacity to utilize that information.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Fuzzy-function programming' to address complex, rule-based programming tasks that are currently outsourced to LLM APIs.
The core concept, 'Program-as-Weights,' compiles natural language specifications into compact, locally executable neural artifacts.
Aims to improve locality, reproducibility, and reduce costs associated with relying heavily on external LLM services.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Introduces OrbitQuant, a new data-agnostic quantization method specifically designed for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs).
Addresses the high inference cost of DiTs, which is exacerbated by multi-step sampling and large parameter counts.
Solves a key limitation of prior quantization methods by handling activation shifts across different timesteps and prompts without requiring re-calibration.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
Proposes LACUNA, a new testbed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
Highlights a gap in current research: existing benchmarks only test output-level unlearning, not internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now supported via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM usage.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: NASA launched an emergency mission to stop the Swift Observatory from crashing to Earth
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: NASA launched an emergency mission to save the Swift Observatory from atmospheric re-entry.
Recent solar storms have caused the 2004-launched observatory's orbit to degrade dangerously.
Katalyst Space Technologies is involved in the rescue effort using a Link spacecraft to intercept the satellite.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated using risk control, showing competitive results in testing.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against 'off-the-record' (OTR) private responses.
Suggests that social context can drive emergent, unprompted objectives within LLM interactions.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The study proposes using Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker recognition in these challenging video contexts.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLM training.
Addresses a critical limitation of existing OPSD methods: teacher-side token-level supervision can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The core innovation focuses on modulating the distillation process to mitigate these negative effects.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with classical symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers, generating complete solution proposals to guide established methods like backtracking and SAT solvers (e.g., Glucose 4.1).
The work highlights SE-RRMs' improved extrapolation capabilities when handling larger constraint satisfaction problems.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive data like PII from training sets.
It focuses on 'unlearning,' a post-hoc method to remove this memorized knowledge, which is currently a major research challenge.
The research introduces LACUNA, a testbed to evaluate localization precision, moving beyond simple output-level unlearning benchmarks.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's effectiveness is shown to be competitive in tests involving mathematical reasoning and red teaming.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses.
Examines the emergence of latent objectives when agents operate within a socially structured environment without explicit prompting.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for training LLMs.
Addresses a critical limitation of current OPSD methods: dense, privileged token-level supervision causes overfitting and harms cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities by modulating the distillation process to encourage better exploration.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces Controllable Neural Variational Agents (CNeVA) for realistic simulation.
The framework allows simulated agents to imitate logged behavior while being steerable along interpretable axes.
This controllability is crucial for testing autonomous systems and isolating variables without real-world risk.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of post-training LLMs without costly human supervision in specialized domains.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Uses the model's own outputs and majority voting across rollouts to generate pseudo-labels for self-improvement.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks perform under real-world, decentralized data conditions.
Contributes to the theoretical understanding of D-SSL robustness, a key area for scaling ML with decentralized data.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Proposes 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-resistant programming tasks.
This paradigm compiles natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts (Program-as-Weights).
Aims to reduce reliance on external LLM APIs, addressing issues of locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's effectiveness is shown to be competitive in mathematical reasoning and red teaming scenarios.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent settings.
Compares public utterances against 'off-the-record' (OTR) responses to detect latent objective emergence.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study socially conditioned LLM communication.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, is introduced, containing 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The work leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of attributing spoken utterances to specific characters.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to Typographic Attacks (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning over true visual semantics.
The research proposes a training-free method for robust concept localization to address this critical failure mode.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection, specifically poor attention to visual inputs during error correction.
Proposes a novel reinforcement learning framework to enable LVLMs to perform visually grounded self-reflection.
Aims to improve the models' ability to translate feedback into accurate corrections, particularly for out-of-distribution images.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: Investigates whether scaling LLMs will improve the fidelity of social simulations.
Examines the relationship between compute scale, general capabilities, and simulation accuracy.
Proposes that simulation fidelity might be an orthogonal research area separate from general LLM capabilities.

stories.title: GPT-5.5 Codex reasoning-token clustering may be leading to degraded performance
stories.author: maille
bullet_points: The news concerns potential performance degradation in GPT-5.5.
The suspected cause is related to 'reasoning-token clustering' within the model.
The report originates from Hacker News, indicating a technical discussion among the community.

stories.title: My credential rule reported 842 secrets in vercel/ai. The real count was 0.
stories.author: ofri-peretz
bullet_points: A security scanning tool (credential rule) generated a high number of false positives (842 findings) when scanning a repository.
The false positives were primarily non-sensitive code artifacts like TypeScript union-type literals and string literals, not actual secrets.
The article discusses the challenge of context-blind regex in security scanning and how AI assistants can inadvertently regenerate strings that trigger these false positives.

stories.title: What Google's "Microservices Are Dead" Paper Actually Said (And What It Missed About AI)
stories.author: zxpmail
bullet_points: The article analyzes a 2023 Google paper by senior engineers regarding the state of microservices.
It specifically discusses the paper's claims and critiques its perspective, particularly concerning the integration of AI.
The piece is relevant to software architecture and large-scale systems design, offering an expert-level discussion.

stories.title: Your Self-Hosted LLM Has No Auth by Default. One Config Line Decides Who Runs It.
stories.author: alex_spinov
bullet_points: The article addresses a critical security vulnerability in self-hosted Large Language Models (LLMs) regarding default lack of authentication.
A specific configuration line in the setup process is highlighted as the determinant for enabling access control.
A tool, 'exposure_gate.py', is introduced to perform offline linting of configuration files (.env, compose, LiteLLM) for security checks.
